races.name: William Hill Epic Boost Fillies' Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Forest Berry
runners_data.note: Has won her last two starts with strong staying form, and Sir Mark Prescott's handling of juvenile fillies at this track is a significant angle; wears headgear (h) and goes on standard going, but STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is technically a prominent horse shown leading — she may be racing out of true role, though her recent wins suggest she can dictate from the front competently enough.|

runners_data.name: Woodhay Wayfarer
runners_data.note: Won last time over this exact 8f trip on Good going and steps up in class here; Billy Loughnane is a high-calibre booking and 30 days off poses no obvious concern; a genuine prominent racer with course-and-distance winning form who should slot in naturally behind Forest Berry.|

runners_data.name: Greek Symphony
runners_data.note: Three wins and places from five starts, consistent performer who landed a 7f Standard success and has the repetitive placed form to suggest she handles this trip well; Mason Paetel's 3lb claim is relevant on what is 133lbs, and Oliver Cole's stable is in decent nick at 2/8 over 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Pequenita
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a significant jockey upgrade and Andrew Balding's yard commands respect, but this filly's natural instinct is to race up with the pace — with the prominent slots already congested by Forest Berry and the genuine two, she is likely to find herself further back than suits and her modest 0W1P sim-going record underlines the task.|

runners_data.name: Crazy Cubana
runners_data.note: Won on her debut over 6f on Good and has shown ability, but her two most recent runs (17th at Goodwood, 0 latest) suggest she is currently out of form; Ed Walker has a reasonable 14-day strike rate but this filly is a front-runner by nature who will struggle to assert her preferred position in this field and 37 days off adds uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Magnesium
runners_data.note: John Butler's hold-up filly won on Standard going over 6f but faces a stiffer test stepping up to 1m here; 42 days off is the longest absence in the field and Rossa Ryan is a capable jockey, but a slow-run race on a flat track is the worst scenario for a genuine hold-up type who needs fractions to run into.|

runners_data.name: Attack Attack
runners_data.note: Clearly a hold-up horse whose best effort in recent form is a modest 5th at Goodwood, and no sim-going record makes assessment harder; Liam Wright's 3lb claim helps the weight, but the 44-day break combined with a form string of 0035 signals she is finding it difficult to raise her game sufficiently in nursery company.|

runners_data.name: Golden Oasis
runners_data.note: Ran an unnamed position (U) last time suggesting a setback of some kind, which demands caution; Rob Hornby takes the ride but Robert Edwards's 0/1 14-day record is weak and this natural front-runner will be displaced by the traffic ahead, making her true prominent style effectively redundant in this shape.|

races.paceDynamic: Forest Berry is the one confirmed front runner here and, with a clear lead from the gates on this flat Kempton polytrack mile, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop without meaningful pressure — Sir Mark Prescott's filly has won twice recently and has the profile to coast into a rhythm that suits her stamina. Behind her, Woodhay Wayfarer and Greek Symphony are genuine prominent types likely to track close, while Pequenita, Crazy Cubana, and Golden Oasis are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who cannot all get their preferred positions and will be forced to either race wide in a bunched group or sit slightly further back than ideal. Magnesium and Attack Attack are the true hold-up types, but with a likely moderate pace set by a single uncontested leader, they face a stiff ask to close ground from off the pace around a flat, galloping track that offers no false pace to exploit. The race shape strongly favours those travelling prominently behind Forest Berry — horses who can latch onto a genuine rhythm, avoid the traffic in the redistribution squeeze, and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out rather than a late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Forest Berry Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Forest Berry leads uncontested at a fair pace and the field strings out into a rhythm that suits prominent trackers.
scenarios.body: Forest Berry bowls along on the front end with Woodhay Wayfarer and Greek Symphony tucking in close, and the race is run at a metronomic clip that gradually exposes the field's staying limitations; horses who travel fluently in the slipstream are perfectly placed turning in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Forest Berry sets a fraction too strong and one of the close-up prominent types picks her off inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Greek Symphony or Woodhay Wayfarer race in a perfect stalking position and use their superior turn of foot to collar the leader late; both have the form to suggest they can produce a decisive effort once switched off in a small field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Helps Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the glut of displaced prominent types crowd the pace and create a messy early scramble that briefly inflates fractions.
scenarios.body: Should Pequenita, Crazy Cubana or Golden Oasis push forward regardless, the pace quickens to a degree that flattens the front-runners and allows the genuine hold-up horses to stay on past tired rivals; Magnesium has won on standard-to-slow Kempton-style surfaces and is the most credible beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Forest Berry crawls and the field concertinas into a bunched group that produces a sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A compressed field suits whoever has the sharpest acceleration on the day rather than the best tactical position, and the standard-to-slow going may blunt the advantage of the hold-up horses who need a true pace to run into.

watchPoints.text: Forest Berry's headgear (hood) and STYLE_FIT tag mean punters should monitor whether she genuinely settles and leads smoothly — if she pulls hard or is outpaced early by the displaced prominent types pushing forward, the entire race shape changes.

Pequenita, Crazy Cubana, and Golden Oasis are all natural front-runners who cannot all get their preferred positions — watch the first two furlongs for jostling or wider-than-ideal running that could compromise their races and briefly inflate the pace.

Magnesium's 42-day absence is the longest in the field; watch for any signs of ring rustiness in the warm-up or early strides, as a hold-up horse returning from six weeks off needs to travel fluently to have any chance in a likely-steady-paced race.

The going report confirms Standard to Slow for this race — slightly deeper than typical Kempton AW conditions, which will marginally blunt finishing speed and could slightly extend the advantage of horses travelling prominently rather than those relying on a late burst.

races.name: William Hill London Mile Series Final Handicap Stakes (Series Final - Qualified Horses Only)

runners_data.name: Two Tempting
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here with the clearest route to the rail; handled this track and trip well (three STA starts in form string) but races from a prominent style that slightly undercuts its finishing kick once headed — the question is whether an uncontested lead can see it home.

runners_data.name: Popmaster
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with solid Kempton form and a tidy record on similar going (9/15 sim-going), though a 28-day break from a yard whose 14-day record is unremarkable at 7/40 gives mild pause; tracks the pace prominently and needs that platform to be sustained into the straight.

runners_data.name: Supido
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose sim-going record on AW standard is very thin (3/15, 0W0P), and the step back up to 8f after recent 7f outings is an open question; headgear (t) may sharpen its early response but it will need daylight in a crowded straight.

runners_data.name: Nikovo
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy book, progressive form (854331) and strong sim-going credentials (9/15); hold-up style needs something to chase but Murphy's positional instinct at Kempton gives this horse a live each-way profile if any real gallop materialises.

runners_data.name: Cavolo Nero
runners_data.note: In form and in-trip — two wins at 8f on standard going recently (5/13, 2W5P) — and Harry Eustace's yard is cold over 14 days (0/14) but the horse's own evidence is compelling; a prominent racer who should slot in just behind Two Tempting and time a challenge from there.

runners_data.name: The Liffey
runners_data.note: Exceptional record at this trip and surface (8/15 sim-going, 4W4P) and the form string 115112 signals a horse in excellent nick; wears headgear (tb), travels from hold-up or just off the pace, and the trainer's stable is quiet but the horse's own profile is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Percy's Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has won at 7f on this surface and hit the frame at 8f on AW; headgear (p) is retained and he has been out 18 days, but the sim-going return (4/15, 1W3P) is modest and trainer 14-day form is a blank (0/4).

runners_data.name: Dingle
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse whose true style is obscured by redistribution into the midfield band on this map — the form recently is poor (173000) and 72 days off is the longest absence in this field; sim-going record at 10/15 is the weakest, making this a tough revival assignment.

runners_data.name: I'm Workin On It
runners_data.note: Strong sim-going profile (13/15, 4W7P) and a win at this trip; wears headgear (p) and Rod Millman's yard is ticking over (4/26), but 68 days since last run is a significant fitness query that prominent-tracking tactics will quickly expose.

runners_data.name: Exposure
runners_data.note: A true prominent racer whose natural position could not be held in this congested field — John & Thady Gosden send it out 17 days fresh with Benoit de la Sayette aboard, but the sim-going record (1/7, 0W0P) is conspicuously sparse and the style displacement reduces its win probability.

runners_data.name: Warrior Mode
runners_data.note: Won at this trip and surface (5/7 sim-going, 2W3P) and Sir Mark Prescott's patient preparation over 24 days carries authority; a prominent-style runner who should find a decent early position in the second rank and has the class to quicken from there.

runners_data.name: Blue Prince
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on Good and has placed four times in similar going (7/15, 0W4P on STA); a natural prominent type squeezed out of that position by the sheer number of pace-pressing rivals — the style displacement is a real tactical handicap in a field this densely packed up front.

runners_data.name: Victory Ace
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a hat-trick of wins including three at this trip on Standard (8/10, 4W5P), operating off OR 89 with a career peak in form; Finley Marsh takes over, and the hold-up style could be ideally placed if the prominent pack produces any meaningful tempo.

runners_data.name: Vincent Rocks
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose true style is compressed into the midfield tier on this map due to a surplus of rear-end types; Warren Fentiman (3lb claim) returns after 42 days and the sim-going record (3/8, 1W2P) is modest — visor (v) retained but the redistribution from natural style is a tangible disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Two Tempting is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with a clean break from the stalls, should secure an uncontested lead through Kempton's long back straight, setting a steady, controllable tempo on Standard to Slow ground. Popmaster, Cavolo Nero, Percy's Lad, Warrior Mode and I'm Workin On It all carry genuine prominent intentions, meaning the race shape will be congested in the first third as those five compete for the positions directly behind Two Tempting — the field holds more prominent types than can all settle in that tier, with Cavolo Nero, Warrior Mode and Popmaster most likely to actually secure the rail spots behind the leader given their recent form and class. This controlled, single-pacemaker dynamic over a flat mile on AW typically compresses the field into a group through the home turn, producing a tactical affair where the pace injection into Kempton's long straight is decisive. The race shape favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and sustain a powerful, well-timed run through the final two furlongs — pure hold-up closers will need a genuine tempo to close on and, with the pace so thinly sourced, that is far from guaranteed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tempting dictates an unchallenged, honest gallop and the winner travels in the first four throughout
scenarios.body: Two Tempting sets fractions that are controlled but not slow enough to produce a sprint finish, meaning horses who travel prominently use their energy efficiently and hit the rising ground in the straight with reserves intact; the long Kempton straight rewards those who quicken from a settled position rather than those making up ground from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl, Sprint Home
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack checks each other's stride and the pace is so slow that the final two furlongs become a pure speed test
scenarios.body: A dawdling tempo through the back straight turns this into a dash for home off a near-standing start, suiting horses with a sharp sectional change and class to quicken from a compact group; the lack of genuine gallopers ensures the field arrives at the two-furlong pole in a heap.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tempting is left alone at a genuine clip and the pack fails to organise a coordinated challenge in time
scenarios.body: Two Tempting, untroubled and in a rhythm on going it handles, extends its advantage turning in and the prominent pack — fractured by its own crowding — fails to coordinate a cohesive move until it is too late; Kempton's flat profile removes the climbs that would normally expose a front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack sets a strong enough pace to string the field out and true hold-up horses find daylight in the straight
scenarios.body: A genuinely run mile with a pressured middle section would create a gap for runners held up conserving energy, but this scenario is undermined by the redistribution of Dingle, Vincent Rocks and Exposure — none are true rear-of-field closers by nature — and the single front-runner makes a truly searching pace unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Two Tempting holds a uniquely clear route to the front in a 14-runner field — watch whether it secures total isolation or gets hustled by Cavolo Nero and Warrior Mode in the first furlong, as that determines the entire pace shape.

Victory Ace's three-win hat-trick at this course and trip on Standard going makes it the standout course specialist, and if Finley Marsh can find a position three or four off the pace in the home straight the horse's sectionals suggest it will be the fastest finisher.

The cluster of prominent-style runners — Popmaster, Percy's Lad, I'm Workin On It, Exposure, Blue Prince — will jostle for positions in the first half-mile; monitor early stride patterns as any crowding or interference behind Two Tempting could burn energy from the very horses relying on a prominent pitch.

The Liffey's 38-day break and headgear (tb) warrant scrutiny in the paddock — it has four wins at this trip and surface but trainer Hayley Burton has a blank 14-day record (0/3) and a flat preparation would undermine what looks a strong profile on paper.

Going reported as Standard to Slow — marginally slower than pure Standard — which marginally favours stamina over raw speed; watch whether horses dropping from 10f (Cavolo Nero, historically) handle the shorter trip more crisply or whether that stamina edge comes into play late.

races.name: William Hill September Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Dubai Future
runners_data.note: A decade-old stalwart of Saeed bin Suroor's string who races from well off the pace; the step up from 1m2f to 1m4f here at Goodwood last time yielded only a ninth, and at ten years old his best form on the AW feels some way behind him — Jack Mitchell's hold-up tactics will depend heavily on the tempo being genuinely demanding.

runners_data.name: Almeric
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's consistent four-year-old has placed in five of his last six outings at around a mile and a quarter, though his sole win came on Soft ground and he now steps up in trip; Rob Hornby should be able to park him prominently just off Gethin, which suits his race-shape given the expected tempo.

runners_data.name: Constitution Hill
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's nine-year-old boasts back-to-back wins at Kempton over 1m2f on the AW but has not run for 164 days and steps up to 1m4f; by nature he wants to race close to the pace, but with Gethin, Tornado Alert and Almeric all holding similar territory, he will be pushed wider in the pack than ideal, tempering confidence despite his Kempton course form.

runners_data.name: Gethin
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows's four-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner in this field and Callum Rodriguez can take a simple lead from the outset; his sole win at Kempton over a mile on Standard ground reads promisingly for this surface, and dictating uncontested fractions over 1m4f plays directly to his strengths, though his OR of 117 has yet to be fully tested at this trip.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Arras
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up performer won over 1m2f at Goodwood on Good but was beaten a long way out in the Listed race last time; Rossa Ryan will be required to find his way through on a compact Kempton circuit from the rear, and the slow tempo projected here leaves him with least to gain from the race shape.

runners_data.name: Tornado Alert
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this Suroor four-year-old who has won at a mile on both Soft and Standard surfaces and looks the most natural horse to slot in directly behind Gethin; his prominent style is well-suited to the expected pace scenario, and proximity to the leader throughout gives him every chance to score if he can see out the 1m4f trip, which remains a question having not raced beyond 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Warrant Holder
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's four-year-old has won on Standard ground at 1m2f and 1m at Kempton, and Benoit de la Sayette is an able handler; however, despite being a natural front-runner, the density of prominent types means he is unlikely to secure that forward berth and will need to switch off in a role that does not play to his instincts — his headgear (tongue-tie) hints at management rather than transformation.

races.paceDynamic: Gethin is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for that position, Callum Rodriguez can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over Kempton's flat, right-handed 1m4f loop. Tornado Alert and Almeric are the next most naturally prominent types and will likely track Gethin through the early stages, creating an organised, single-file procession rather than a contested pace battle. The Standard to Slow conditions will suppress sectional times and compress the field, making it harder for hold-up horses like Dubai Future and Pride Of Arras to generate the sustained momentum they need from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit within two lengths of Gethin and respond when he quickens — or press him into submission entering the straight; the field holds more prominent/front-running types than can all get their natural position, with Gethin best placed to lead and Tornado Alert most likely to secure the position just behind, while Warrant Holder and Constitution Hill, genuine front-runners by nature, are unlikely to achieve that berth and will be inconveniently shuffled back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gethin Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Gethin sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the race is decided by who tracks him closest.
scenarios.body: Gethin dictates the fractions from the front, Tornado Alert and Almeric slot in on his heels, and the race resolves as a sprint from the two-furlong pole where proximity to pace is decisive. Horses who have sat within two lengths of the leader throughout hold every advantage on this flat, turning track at a slow tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Gethin's early control lulls the field into a crawl that explodes into a furious final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow tempo can produce a bunched finish where high-class hold-up horses do find room to deliver a finishing effort, but Standard to Slow conditions are more likely to sustain than accelerate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Held-Up Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Gethin goes too hard early on a Slow surface and blows up inside the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Sustained fractions on an energy-sapping surface can exhaust front-runners, and Dubai Future or Pride Of Arras could sweep through late, but Gethin's class and the measured pace projection make this an unlikely outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Duels, Fresh Winner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Tornado Alert or Almeric apply enough pressure to Gethin that a fresher or more relaxed rival exploits the attrition.
scenarios.body: A pressured pace would open the door for a closer, but with no horse likely to seriously contest Gethin's lead in the early stages, genuine front-end pressure is a low-probability trigger.

watchPoints.text: Tornado Alert is likely to secure the position immediately behind Gethin without contest — if Oisin Murphy slots him into that spot early, he will be first to pounce when the leader is challenged and should be tracked throughout.

Constitution Hill has not raced for 164 days and steps up in trip; watch how sharply Billy Loughnane asks him to be competitive early, as a rusty start could leave him stranded in traffic on a track that offers limited room to weave.

Warrant Holder's natural instinct is to race prominently, but the field configuration will likely push him into an unfamiliar holding role — watch for signs of restlessness or early cover-seeking that could see him use energy unnecessarily before the straight.

The Standard to Slow surface at Kempton AW today is confirmed across all races on the card — any horse whose best form is on a true Standard surface may find the ground slightly more taxing than expected, and closing runs from the rear are statistically harder to land in these conditions.

Dubai Future's ten-year age and recent ninth at 1m4f at Goodwood should be noted if he drifts in the market — Jack Mitchell may attempt to position him closer than his typical hold-up role to compensate for the expected lack of pace pressure.

races.name: William Hill Sirenia Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Adaay of Scarlett
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 106 and genuine gate-to-wire type with Hugo Palmer in strong recent form (2/29 T14); four consecutive runner-up finishes on good ground suggest rivals have caught up with her, and she will need to dominate from stall one if that pattern is to reverse on this slower surface.

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's colt has proven AW/similar-going form (1W1P on Standard) and the step back to six furlongs suits after a muddling run in the Moyglare; Finley Marsh takes over but the profile — prominent, stays six well, acts on the surface — fits this pace-heated scenario neatly.

runners_data.name: Moonrise
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three runs and a Kempton winner on Standard going already in the book; Andrew Balding's colt has the exact profile this race shape rewards — patient enough to track a hot pace and strong enough to sustain through the final furlong — and 42 days off should have freshened him without dulling his edge.

runners_data.name: Social Symbol
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner who wants to bowl along in front, but an OR of just 96 means he is giving weight in class terms to almost the entire field; the danger is getting into a battle with Adaay of Scarlett and Nicely early, which could render him vulnerable to a prominent racer with more class in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: Tawakal
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (just two runs) with a win over this course and distance already; the Crisfords hold the horse in decent regard and Jack Mitchell knows the yard well, though the step up into Group 3 company on a slower surface is an unknown — makes most appeal if the race is run at a steadier tempo.

runners_data.name: Bated Benevolence
runners_data.note: Front-running winner on Standard going (sim-going 1W1P) and is unexposed, but an OR of 86 leaves him well out of his depth on official ratings; Benoit de la Sayette will likely find him outpaced by the superior early pace of Adaay of Scarlett and Social Symbol, forcing him back from his natural position.

runners_data.name: Efsixteen
runners_data.note: Won his only start at five furlongs on good ground but the headgear flag (hg:t — tongue tie) is worth noting; stepping into Group 3 company having only contested a novice contest is a tall ask, and being a confirmed front-runner in a field stacked with pace means he is likely to race in a difficult position or use too much energy early.

runners_data.name: Evenfall
runners_data.note: An unbeaten two-year-old (1/6f/GOO, 1/5f/GOO) for George Boughey whose natural style is prominent but has been pushed back in the mapping due to the field's front-runner surplus — in practice Billy Loughnane will likely try to hold a position just off the leaders, making Evenfall a potential beneficiary if the pace blows up and he threads through cleanly.

runners_data.name: Nicely
runners_data.note: Won twice including over six furlongs on soft and good ground and is a genuine pace angle; Kevin Philippart De Foy's filly has legitimate front-running credentials and Rowan Scott is capable, though getting into a three- or four-wide battle in the first furlong with Adaay of Scarlett and Social Symbol risks her being outgunned before the race begins in earnest.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sun
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's colt has a decent form figure (2/5f/GOO) but also a blot (14th on soft, 7th) and his trainer has had no winners from 14 runners in the past fortnight; likely to be chasing the pace from a midfield position given the prominent runners ahead of him, and at OR 94 needs a significant step forward to threaten.

races.paceDynamic: Five confirmed front-runners — Adaay of Scarlett, Social Symbol, Nicely, Bated Benevolence, and Efsixteen — will ignite an unrelenting pace from the gates over Kempton's straight six, and with Standard to Slow conditions adding drag, the early sectionals will be punishing for those who burn fuel fighting for position. Social Symbol and Nicely in particular have gate-to-wire form over this course configuration, but all five will be jostling for the same real estate in the first two furlongs, creating significant friction and ensuring no one leads for free. The field holds more front-running types than can all secure their preferred positions, with Adaay of Scarlett (highest OR among the pace horses) and Social Symbol (course winner) best placed to actually carve out the rail berth, while Bated Benevolence and Efsixteen are likely to be bumped back into a chasing role against their instincts. This race shape emphatically favours prominent-to-midfield horses with a sustained late kick — runners who can sit just off the carnage and collar a flattening leader in the final furlong will be ideally placed, with Moonrise and Agamemnon the profiles to watch.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners burn each other out through a blistering early half and the Standard to Slow surface extracts maximum toll on the leaders.
scenarios.body: The front-runners tie each other up from the off, leaving Adaay of Scarlett or Social Symbol fighting for air at the two-furlong pole while prominent-to-midfield raiders pounce late; Moonrise and Agamemnon, both with form at this trip on similar going, are best positioned to pick up the pieces with a sustained gallop through to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacer Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Adaay of Scarlett or Social Symbol secures an uncontested lead after the initial scrimmage and the other front-runners check and slot in behind rather than fight.
scenarios.body: A single leader who avoids the worst of the early battle conserves enough to hold a clear advantage turning for home on this flat, straight track with no bend to help closers; the Standard to Slow surface rewards a horse that rations energy early and gallops relentlessly rather than quickening sharply.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Hangs On
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fractionally more honest than brutal and a well-positioned prominent horse tracks the melee before asserting from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Moonrise, with a win at Kempton on similar going already banked and Oisin Murphy in the saddle, is the prototype for this shape — sitting just behind the skirmish and producing a clean, sustained run to the line; Agamemnon's Group 2 form and proven ability on AW-type going makes it the second beneficiary if it secures a clear passage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If widespread trouble in running at the two-to-three furlong mark — the predicted congestion zone — results in interference that scrambles the expected finishing order.
scenarios.body: A runner that has a clean passage through untroubled by the front-rank scrimmage emerges with a clear advantage; Evenfall (unbeaten in two and covering ground in the slipstream) or Shimmering Sun could benefit if the pace horses collide figuratively or literally and create a gap.

watchPoints.text: Adaay of Scarlett, Social Symbol, and Nicely all want the same rail position in the opening furlong — watch for a three-way bump-and-grind that disrupts all of them and opens a gap for midfield horses to exploit.
Moonrise is 42 days off the track and a bounce after two sharp wins is a known risk; watch for signs of greenness or sluggish early pace in the market that might signal she is not at her sharpest.

Efsixteen's step from a novice five-furlong win to Group 3 six furlongs on a slower surface is extremely steep — if his early pace is absorbed by the front-runner war he may find himself in no-man's-land with nowhere to go.

Evenfall's redistribution from prominent to effective hold-up means Billy Loughnane will need a clean run through the pack from a position that does not suit — watch for him to get caught in the two-to-three furlong traffic zone flagged in the pace data.

Standard to Slow going at Kempton AW confirmed across the card — every runner's form on faster surfaces should be mentally discounted one grade, which particularly benefits Agamemnon and Bated Benevolence who have already shown they handle similar conditions.

races.name: William Hill Price Boosts Every Day Fillies' Handicap Stakes (London Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Zighy
runners_data.note: A prominent racer for George Boughey with Billy Loughnane up, proven winner at Standard going (1/6f/STA) and placed multiple times over 6f at Goodwood; the handicapper has her on a manageable mark and she is 15 days fresh which is a typical Boughey pattern; the contested pace is exactly what she needs travelling just off the leaders.

runners_data.name: Lady Roxby
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has been well beaten on Good ground in recent starts (7s and 9s), but her sole placed effort in similar going came on Standard AW (3/6f/STA); 43 days off is a concern for a horse without obvious return-to-form indicators, and the pace will need to be genuinely fierce for her to land a blow from the back.

runners_data.name: Powdering
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who won on Good at 6f in her last win and has placed twice on AW; six runs at similar going yield no wins though, and Seamus Cronin's 5lb claim is useful ballast; her recent form string is inconsistent and she needs a fast pace collapse to get competitive from her deep draw position.

runners_data.name: Tarot
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner from Roger Varian's yard, ridden by Ross Coakley; won at 6f on Standard AW (1/6f/STA) and has course form, but her last four have seen her finish 6th-7th — she may need to set the pace to show her best and could be vulnerable if she gets into a protracted duel with Veil Of Clouds; headgear note (hg:h) adds an interest angle.

runners_data.name: Eskimo Pie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from Jane Chapple-Hyam's yard who won on Good at 6f (1/6f/GOO) and has placed on Standard AW; her record of 0 trainer wins in 11 recent starts (T14:0/11) is a clear caution, and while she has ability, the pace shape needs to really unravel for her to reach the leaders from her typical deep position.

runners_data.name: Shallow
runners_data.note: Versatile profile with a variable headgear record (hg:v) and a genuine hold-up preference, but with so many hold-up types in this field she is one of those pushed forward on the map to midfield — in reality she is likely to end up further back than that natural midfield shows, which limits her winning chance unless the pace is extreme; her form on Good (two 2nds at 6f) is better than on AW.

runners_data.name: Paradise Walk
runners_data.note: A prominent racer from Ralph Beckett's powerful yard, ridden by Rossa Ryan, with two wins over 5-6f on Good (1/5f/GOO, 1/6f/GOO) and three placed efforts at similar going; 39 days off and a slight blinkered headgear flag (hg:b) are worth noting, but this is a horse that handles a contested pace well and could be the sleeper of the field at a likely bigger price.

runners_data.name: Veil Of Clouds
runners_data.note: The key pace horse with Oisin Murphy booked, unbeaten at Kempton AW in her course win (1/6f/STA) with three further placed efforts on the same surface — this is very much her track; turf headgear flag (hg:t) noted; she may not have to work overly hard to get to the front, and Murphy's masterclass in pace management is the single biggest tactical variable in the race.

runners_data.name: Calling A Star
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with two wins at 6f including on Standard AW (1/6f/STA) and on Good (1/6f/GOO); 38 days off and a form string showing 7th and 4th in her last two after her wins signals she may not be as sharp as at peak, but she has the profile of a horse who can travel handy and challenge turning into the straight.

runners_data.name: Lope El Fuego
runners_data.note: Prominent type who was well beaten in her last two (9th, 9th) and has not run for 58 days — the layoff is notable and form tailed off markedly after a promising early-season win; Warren Greatrex's 3/11 T14 rate is modest and there is limited encouragement from her recent Goodwood outings; needs to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Rumble Ruby
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer — genuinely used to racing in the first two or three — but the density of pace horses in this field means she is unlikely to access that position freely and could find herself racing slightly against her instincts; her form shows three places in six runs on similar going and Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim helps on weight, but her chance is tempered by the likely positional compromise.

races.paceDynamic: Tarot and Veil Of Clouds are the two confirmed front-runners in an 11-runner field, and with both likely to assert for the early lead, a genuinely contested pace is expected from the outset on this Standard to Slow Kempton AW surface. Oisin Murphy aboard Veil Of Clouds gives that side real quality, and the likely duel between the two will set an honest, pressure-filled gallop through the first two furlongs before the field settles into its shape. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all find their natural positions — Rumble Ruby is a true prominent racer who is likely to be shuffled back from her preferred berth, and Shallow, naturally a hold-up horse, has also been redistributed due to congestion behind the pace. This race shape — two genuine leaders pressing each other on a surface that is slower than advertised — favours prominent-to-midfield horses who travel fluidly just off a pressured pace and finish strongly without needing to make their own move, giving the edge to the prominent and tracking profiles over true closers or those forced out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Trackers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Tarot and Veil Of Clouds fight for the lead and set a strong enough gallop to drain each other, horses travelling just off the pace in the slipstream benefit.
scenarios.body: The sustained pressure from the front two creates an honest, draining tempo that sets up runners who have been covered up in third to sixth, with the slower-than-standard surface compounding the toll on the leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Veil Of Clouds Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Veil Of Clouds, ridden by Oisin Murphy, asserts early supremacy and Tarot fails to sustain the challenge, Murphy dictates a manageable gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: A soft lead on a Standard to Slow surface suits a front-runner who can control the fractions, and Veil Of Clouds' strong Kempton AW record and course-winning form makes her the obvious beneficiary of any easing in the pace battle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fierce and the prominent types all use each other up, a horse coming from further back can sweep through late.
scenarios.body: Eskimo Pie or Lady Roxby would need the first five to tie up badly, which is possible on the slower surface, but the redistribution of Shallow and the broader congestion means few true hold-up horses are well positioned to exploit this.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leaders Win
scenarios.trigger: If Tarot and Veil Of Clouds strike an early truce and the pace proves slower than expected, the front two could dictate and kick clear.
scenarios.body: A steadier gallop on a sluggish surface could allow one or both leaders to control their own destiny and hold the prominent types at bay, with Murphy's race-reading on Veil Of Clouds the most dangerous version of this shape.

watchPoints.text: Veil Of Clouds and Tarot — watch the first furlong closely to see which establishes the lead; if Veil Of Clouds gets a soft lead uncontested, Murphy's tactical advantage becomes enormous and the race shape shifts dramatically toward Scenario B.

Rumble Ruby — her natural prominent style is compromised by the field's pace density; if she burns energy fighting for position in the early stages, her finishing effort is likely to be shorter than her form suggests.

Shallow — despite being mapped to midfield, she is a true hold-up horse and is likely to be further back than her map position implies; her winning chance depends on pace that unravels far more than this field's constitution typically allows.

Paradise Walk — 39 days off for Ralph Beckett and blinkers noted; Beckett's runners often return fresh and Ryan is a reliable pilot in handicap company; if she is spot-on fitness-wise, her prominent profile suits the likely shape well and she could outrun her probable starting price.

Standard to Slow surface is slower than the race card's stated "Standard" going — horses with proven AW Kempton form (Veil Of Clouds in particular) hold a meaningful advantage over those whose recent runs have been on Good turf, where sectionals and surface demands differ substantially.

races.name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Haku
runners_data.note: Strong record on standard going at similar trips (4W6P in 15 sim-going runs) and recent Kempton AW form is relevant, though a hold-up style needs the pace to be genuine enough to close into — seven days since last run is fine for a lightly-framed type.

runners_data.name: Astro King
runners_data.note: Only 1 placing from 15 runs on similar going is a damning statistic; headgear (p) hasn't unlocked him lately and a 9-year-old dropping back from turf to AW with Nader up looks short of convincing reasons to back.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: Trainer David Evans in form (T14: 2/19), blinkers fitted (v), and the 7lb claim from McDonnell is meaningful in a tight handicap; has won at 10f on good but this step to 12f AW on standard-to-slow is new territory — form figures of 1,5,8,8 away from that trip suggest the trip is the key question.

runners_data.name: Whitcombe Rockstar
runners_data.note: Already proven over 12f on standard going with two wins at that combination in his last five; 72-day absence is not unusual for Burke's yard and the TV headgear suggests they want him switched on — genuine prominent type who gets his natural position here.

runners_data.name: Topteam
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, giving Murphy total control from flag to finish; 98-day absence is a concern at the weights and his sole turf start at Kempton STA was only 1W1P in 3 sim-going runs, but the tactical advantage of unopposed lead is enormous.

runners_data.name: Incensed
runners_data.note: Amanda Perrett sends a 5-year-old in fair recent fettle (placed three times in last 5 including 2nd at 12f on standard), though a hold-up style on a flat AW track with a modest pace is not ideal and T14 figures are quiet.

runners_data.name: Majestic
runners_data.note: Jack Channon in a small purple patch (T14: 2/18) and the 8-year-old does stay well, but his true racing style is hold-up and he is shuffled into midfield here purely by force of numbers — that means he is unlikely to be back far enough to deliver his trademark late challenge.

runners_data.name: Primo Lara
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's 5-year-old has been in excellent form winning his last two, but he is a genuine wait-and-pounce type whose best runs come from the back of the field; crowded here by several rivals with the same instinct, so Billy Loughnane will have to adapt his tactics from his natural rear-of-field game.

runners_data.name: Tiernan
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine sends a lightly-weighted 4-year-old with back-to-back placed efforts; inherently a hold-up horse at heart, he is squeezed into midfield on the map by weight of numbers — the concern is whether Rossa Ryan can find clear daylight through a congested home straight from a position that isn't truly his horse's own.

runners_data.name: Elsass
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston yard in form (T14: 5/39) and the 4-year-old has shown ability winning at 11f on good, but his real preference is to come from off the pace and standard-to-slow conditions with a controlled pace are not his friend; mapped forward out of necessity, not out of nature.

runners_data.name: Sudu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 4-year-old has a single course win at 12f on good and Rowan Scott can be tactically astute; the prominent style should see him placed naturally behind the leader, and while the T14 run rate (5/17) is encouraging, he has posted only one win in his last six and the form line has been inconsistent.

races.paceDynamic: Topteam is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Oisin Murphy aboard for Balding, should settle comfortably into a lone lead on standard-to-slow Kempton AW over 1m4f, dictating an honest but controllable gallop without any genuine challenger to his position. King's Code and Whitcombe Rockstar are the two confirmed prominent racers who will track Topteam through the first half, creating a modest two-deep pressure behind the leader rather than anything that destabilises the pace. The race shape is therefore a classic lone-leader affair on a flat track — the pace will be sustainable rather than searching, meaning stamina reserves will be intact turning for home and the sprint to the line will matter. This strongly favours Topteam himself if he retains enough petrol, or the two prominent types who can track and pounce, over any genuine hold-up horse needing a searching gallop to be produced late. Several runners — Majestic, Primo Lara, Tiernan and Elsass — are true hold-up horses redistributed forward on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded; in a race of this shape they are unlikely to secure their natural position and their finishing kicks will depend on a pace that may not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Topteam Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Topteam dictates a steady-to-honest lead unopposed and the winner comes from the front or immediately off the pace.
scenarios.body: Topteam sets a measured gallop on the AW flat and, unchallenged, can organise the race entirely to his own rhythm with Murphy timing the kick from the front; the prominent pair of King's Code and Whitcombe Rockstar sit ideally placed to challenge inside the final two furlongs if the leader is caught.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Collars Leader
scenarios.trigger: If King's Code or Whitcombe Rockstar track Topteam throughout and outsprint him from 2f out as his stamina at this trip is tested after a 98-day break.
scenarios.body: King's Code, back to winning form over 10f on good, steps up to 12f for the first time in a while but has the engine and Alexandra McDonnell's claim to compensate; Whitcombe Rockstar has already won at 12f on standard going and arrives off a 72-day break that often suits Burke runners freshened up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Topteam sets a genuinely fast-enough pace that strings the field out and leaves a late gap for one of the genuine closers.
scenarios.body: Primo Lara is in excellent form with back-to-back wins and Billy Loughnane can be enterprising, while Haku has strong course and standard-going form; however, neither is truly likely to get far enough back to deliver a classic hold-up finish given the overcrowded rear group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems through the overcrowded midfield and a dawdling pace produce a bunched finish that randomises the outcome.
scenarios.body: The sheer number of hold-up horses redistributed into midfield creates a compression risk rounding the home turn, potentially leaving Incensed or Sudu, both with course experience, a clear run when others are blocked.

watchPoints.text: Topteam's 98-day absence is the single biggest risk to Scenario A — watch the market to see if Balding's stable confidence is reflected at the off, as an undercooked front-runner who ties up late becomes a gift for Whitcombe Rockstar or King's Code.

The five hold-up horses (Majestic, Primo Lara, Tiernan, Elsass, Haku) all competing for the same rear/midfield ground creates a serious traffic risk rounding the home turn — watch for any horse caught wide or pocketed at the two-furlong marker.

Primo Lara arrives on the back of consecutive wins but will be shuffled out of his natural position by the volume of hold-up types; if Billy Loughnane is forced to race too close to the pace, the horse's rhythm could be compromised entirely.

King's Code wears blinkers and has the 7lb claim — watch if Alexandra McDonnell positions him close to Topteam from the off, because if she gets a prominent pitch the claim could prove decisive in a finish that comes down to a tight margin.

Standard-to-slow going at Kempton AW tonight is confirmed across all distances — Astro King's dire record in these conditions (0W0P from 1 sim-going run) makes him very difficult to support regardless of draw or market move.

races.name: William Hill Keep Your Raceday Positive Handicap Stakes (London Stayers' Series Qualifier) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Naval Tribute
runners_data.note: Has won three of his last six including two at Goodwood over 2m, runs in a visor (hg:v) which sharpens his early pace, and with Rossa Ryan aboard is likely to be sent confidently to the front — his style fits this race perfectly and 96 days off the track is the only minor query, though trainer James Owen's recent 2/36 14-day strike-rate doesn't suggest an in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Barenboim
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse partnered by William Cox for Tom Dascombe who has done little of note in five outings over 16f on similar going, finishing 11th, 9th, 8th and 9th in his last four — his sim-going figures of 1W3P are flattering relative to recent efforts and his OR of 75 leaves him with ground to make up off what looks a steady pace.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over on this consistent six-year-old who has placed in all five of his last starts over 2m, all at Goodwood on similar ground — his sim-going record of 6 runs yielding 1W3P underlines his reliability, and his prominent style makes him the natural on-pace threat to Naval Tribute in a small field.

runners_data.name: Betelgeuse
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for S Woods who is naturally suited to making a late run, yet the race shape leaves him likely racing in midfield rather than from the rear; still lightly raced at four with a promising OR of 66, his 14-day turnaround keeps connections' 2/8 recent form relevant and he is unexposed enough over staying trips to surprise.

runners_data.name: Campeona
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old is a hat-trick winner in her last three starts including two over 16f at Goodwood on Good, and her sim-going record (3/8, 0W0P on AW/Slow) raises a flag about surface suitability — that said, her progressive profile and light weight of 126lbs make her the most interesting closer if she adapts, and Prescott's typical patient placing is worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Flash Kozo
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse for Harry Eustace whose natural style involves coming from off the pace, but in this six-runner field over 2m he is unlikely to find the space to race as far back as he would prefer; won over 14f on Standard going at Kempton and has placed three times in his last five, though his current OR of 72 and the packed hold-up division make his role difficult.

races.paceDynamic: Naval Tribute is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with just six runners over 2m on a Standard to Slow Polytrack surface, figures to bowl along at a measured, uncontested gallop that he can fully control from flag to finish. An Bradan Feasa is the only other horse likely to press forward and track Naval Tribute closely, giving the pace a degree of structure but not genuine pressure. The field nominally contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Flash Kozo and Betelgeuse are true come-from-behind horses mapped into midfield positions they are unlikely to secure naturally, while Barenboim and Campeona will be content to track in behind. With Naval Tribute dictating a sustainable tempo unchallenged over this staying trip, the race shape strongly favours horses who can track close to an unhurried pace and pick off the leader in the straight — a prominent-to-midfield tracking profile has the clearest tactical advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Naval Tribute bowls along at a comfortable, unchallenged tempo and his rivals lack the positional speed to close a gap he can manage throughout.
scenarios.body: Naval Tribute sets an honest but sustainable pace over the 2m trip, and any horse content to track within two or three lengths before delivering a challenge in the straight is ideally placed; An Bradan Feasa's pattern of relentlessly making the frame from a prominent position makes him the primary threat.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Runs On Late
scenarios.trigger: If the Standard to Slow surface slows the pace enough that horses held up conserve significant energy and swamp tired leaders in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The slower going amplifies any early expenditure by Naval Tribute, giving genuine hold-up types a late surge opportunity; Campeona, whose progressive form includes closing wins, and Betelgeuse, a true hold-up performer if allowed to race in his natural position, are best placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If An Bradan Feasa applies sustained pressure on Naval Tribute from some way out, turning the race into an attritional test.
scenarios.body: A genuine battle from the 4f pole would drain both principals and potentially open the door for Campeona, who has multiple wins and places at this sort of trip and handles the pace dynamics well from off the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sprints Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Flash Kozo or Barenboim find themselves much closer than expected and can produce a strong sustained challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: Both horses have shown enough form at this distance level to feature if the race unfolds unusually slowly, though Flash Kozo's mapped midfield position is not his natural berth and Barenboim's recent string of poor finishes (9-9-8-3-11) tempers optimism considerably.

watchPoints.text: Naval Tribute has run 96 days off the track and wears a visor — monitor in the paddock and early strides to confirm he travels with his usual fluency, as any reluctance to bowl along would collapse the dominant scenario entirely.

An Bradan Feasa has Oisin Murphy booked and has placed in every recent run — watch whether Murphy elects to sit tight on Naval Tribute's tail or makes an earlier move, as his positioning in the first half-mile will define whether this becomes a true test or a sprint to the line.

Campeona is the lone three-year-old in a field of older horses and her AW/Slow going sim-going record shows no wins or places in three attempts — watch her in the first few furlongs to see if she settles and travels on the surface before committing to her chance.

Flash Kozo and Betelgeuse are both natural hold-up types crowded into a midfield mapping — if both attempt to creep forward to find a cleaner position, mid-race traffic could bunch the field and create a faster than expected pace in the final 6f, altering the dynamics for the front-runners.
